Hi Sam / BlueHarbor Legal — thanks for the quick turnaround and for looping us in. I’m on Redwood’s legal team; following up with concrete answers and the materials you requested.

Controller/Processor framing:
- For the scenario Rishi described (BlueHarbor sending customer data for KYC summarization), the standard approach is for BlueHarbor to be the Controller and Redwood to be the Processor. That aligns with industry practice and keeps customer-facing obligations with BlueHarbor.
- If you have any mixed-flow cases (e.g., Redwood enriching PII and returning enriched records that imply further processing decisions), we can document carve-outs, but the pilot looks like standard processor activity.

SCC module recommendation:
- Given BlueHarbor is likely the Controller, Module 2 (processor-focused SCC clauses) is the typical fit. Practical differences: Module 2 includes explicit processor obligations (security measures, subprocessors, deletion/return timelines) and preserves Controller liability for lawful basis to process. Module 1 has stronger controller-to-controller clauses and is not usually used where one party is purely providing a service.
- We’ll add a short summary paragraph in the SCC matrix highlighting the deletion/retention timelines and subprocessors.

Retention / DPA redlines:
- We can accept a 45-day retention period for pilot data removal requests; please have counsel redline accordingly. Our standard DPA includes 30/90 options but we’re flexible for pilots.

SOC 2: 
- Attaching a secure link to our SOC 2 Type II report (covers access control, encryption in transit & at rest, and change management) — shareable via signed NDA if needed. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-dpa (download requires authenticated access).

Attachments:
- redwood-dpa-draft.pdf (initial, standard DPA)
- scc-module-matrix.xlsx (summary of Module 1 vs Module 2 + recommended language)

Next steps (from Redwood legal / ops):
1) We’ll upload the SOC 2 artifacts to a secure folder and can provision access to your Legal Ops.
2) Rishi/Monica to start VSQ intake; Monica will send the questionnaire link and expected timeline (approx 5 business days to complete initial VSQ).
3) You can send DPA redlines back to me (irene_choi@redwood.ai). We’ll aim for a 2-week review cycle once both sides exchange redlines.

If BlueHarbor prefers a short call between legal teams to speed alignment, I’m happy to set a 30-min slot.

Best regards,
Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference
